## Project Overview

The **UCSB AI Services Evaluation Suite** is a systematic benchmark designed to assess the
capabilities of large language models (LLMs) available through UCSB-managed AI infrastructure.
The goal is to give researchers, students, and staff an objective basis for choosing which
service and model best fits their workload — weighing accuracy, throughput, and availability.

The benchmark covers six task categories drawn from real research computing workflows at UCSB:
**code generation**, **metadata generation**, **literature synthesis**, **data interpretation**,
**OCR/document extraction**, and **vision question answering**.

```{=html}
  </tbody>
</table>

<div class="method-box">
  <strong>Why infrastructure type matters:</strong>
  GRIT and CIT serve all models locally — model weights run on UCSB hardware, so throughput
  is determined by GPU capacity and network load on university servers.
  AICommons routes requests through Amazon Web Services (Bedrock), which provides scalable
  but metered capacity. The same model binary will produce identical outputs on both
  infrastructure types, but throughput (tokens/sec) and latency will differ.
</div>
```

## Benchmark Datasets

Three benchmark datasets were used, covering increasing complexity and modality:

### Dataset v1 — Standard (12 tasks)

```{=html}
<div class="method-box">
  Twelve text-only tasks across four categories. Designed to represent common research data
  workflows: analysing tabular data programmatically, writing structured metadata,
  synthesising scientific abstracts, and interpreting statistical outputs.
  All tasks use a 1–5 scoring scale.
</div>

<table style="width:100%;margin:0.5rem 0">
  <thead><tr><th>Category</th><th>Tasks</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Code Generation</td><td style="text-align:center">3</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Write Python/pandas to filter, aggregate, and summarise a CSV dataset</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Metadata Generation</td><td style="text-align:center">3</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Generate DataCite-compliant JSON metadata records from dataset descriptions</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Literature Synthesis</td><td style="text-align:center">3</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Extract structured information from scientific abstracts (methodology, findings, limitations)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Data Interpretation</td><td style="text-align:center">3</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Multiple-choice: interpret correlation matrices, regression outputs, and SST distributions</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

### Dataset v2 — Harder (12 tasks)

```{=html}
<div class="method-box">
  Same four categories with scientifically more demanding prompts: tasks require numerical
  precision (e.g. computing Pearson correlation to 4 decimal places), anti-hallucination
  reasoning, detection of internal contradictions in abstracts, and advanced statistical
  interpretation (Simpson's paradox, AIC model selection, autocorrelation).
</div>
```

### Multimodal Dataset (6 tasks)

```{=html}
<div class="method-box">
  Vision-language tasks using two historical document images: a 19th-century Spanish
  newspaper scan and a historical catalogue card.
</div>

<table style="width:100%;margin:0.5rem 0">
  <thead><tr><th>Category</th><th>Tasks</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>OCR</td><td style="text-align:center">2</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Extract structured weather table and bibliographic header from newspaper scan</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Document Extraction</td><td style="text-align:center">1</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Extract all fields from a historical catalogue card</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Vision QA</td><td style="text-align:center">3</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Answer specific factual questions about image content (exact match + judge-scored)</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

## Scoring Methodology

All tasks use a **1–5 integer scale**. The scoring method depends on the task category:

```{=html}
<table style="width:100%;margin:1rem 0">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Category</th>
      <th>Scorer Type</th>
      <th>Score 5</th>
      <th>Score 1</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Code Generation</td>
      <td><code>programmatic</code></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Code executes and produces the correct numeric output</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Code fails to run (syntax error / exception)</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Metadata Generation</td>
      <td><code>programmatic</code></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Valid JSON, all required schema keys present, values correct</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Output is not valid JSON</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Data Interpretation</td>
      <td><code>exact match</code></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Correct MCQ letter selected (A/B/C/D)</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Wrong answer</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Literature Synthesis</td>
      <td><code>LLM judge</code></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">All required fields extracted accurately, no hallucinations, valid JSON</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Missing fields, fabricated content, or completely wrong</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>OCR</td>
      <td><code>programmatic + LLM judge</code></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">All table fields correctly extracted (field-accuracy ≥ 90%)</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Cannot parse response or accuracy &lt; 25%</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Document Extraction</td>
      <td><code>LLM judge</code></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">All document fields captured, no hallucinations</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Major omissions or fabrications</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Vision QA</td>
      <td><code>exact match + LLM judge</code></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Correct answer (for exact-match tasks) or full credit from judge</td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Wrong answer</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<div class="method-box">
  <strong>OCR hybrid scoring:</strong> OCR tasks are first scored programmatically
  (field-accuracy comparison against ground-truth rows). If the programmatic score is below 4/5,
  the LLM judge is called as a second opinion, and the <em>higher</em> score wins.
  This gives models the benefit of the doubt for partial extraction.
</div>
```

---

## LLM-as-a-Judge

For tasks requiring subjective evaluation (literature synthesis, OCR, document extraction,
and some vision tasks), model outputs are evaluated by a second LLM acting as a judge.
The judge receives the model output, the original prompt, and a detailed scoring rubric,
then returns a structured JSON response with a score (1–5) and reasoning.

### Judges Used

```{=html}
<table style="width:100%;margin:1rem 0">
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Judge</th><th>Service</th><th>Role</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>gemini-3.5-flash</strong></td>
      <td><span style="color:#6e7681;text-decoration:line-through">DreamLab</span></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Development judge — used during iterative benchmark development for cost efficiency</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong>claude-v4.6-sonnet</strong></td>
      <td><span class="service-badge badge-aicommons">AICommons</span></td>
      <td style="color:#8b949e">Production judge — used for all final benchmark runs; canonical scores on this dashboard</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<div class="method-box">
  <strong>Judge conflict guard:</strong> The evaluation engine prevents a model from judging its own outputs.
  It detects conflicts by exact model name match, cross-service exact match, and 6-character
  family substring matching. If a conflict is detected, the alternative judge is used automatically.<br><br>
  <strong>Dashboard policy:</strong> Where both judges evaluated the same output, the dashboard
  defaults to Claude (production judge) scores. The Model Explorer page provides a toggle
  to view and compare both judge scores for literature synthesis tasks.
</div>
```

---

## Token Budgets & Evaluation Scope

```{=html}
<div class="method-box">
  Each service has a monthly token budget enforced by the evaluation engine.
  Token consumption is tracked atomically across runs in <code>.token_usage.json</code>.
  Judge calls (which consume tokens from the judge's service budget) stop automatically
  when the monthly limit is approached — leaving a safety buffer.<br><br>
  Budgets: GRIT 10M · CIT 10M · AICommons 900K (strict 1M monthly cap with 100K buffer).
</div>
```

---

## Reproducibility

The full evaluation suite is open-source. To reproduce any result:

```{=html}
<div class="method-box">
  <code>uv run python run_eval.py --judge-service aicommons --judge-model claude-v4.6-sonnet</code><br><br>
  The <code>--resume</code> flag skips already-completed <code>(service, model, test_id)</code> triplets,
  making interrupted runs safe to continue.
  The <code>--re-judge</code> flag re-scores stored model outputs with a new judge
  without re-calling target models — useful for comparing judge quality without incurring
  additional inference costs.
</div>
```
